name: captions_add
title: Add captions
description: Places a run of captions in one undoable step: one title per entry, from `start` to `end` seconds, each on a lane above the picture. `style` applies to all of them (its `content` is ignored); without one they look like the window's captions - Hanken Grotesk, weight 600, 0.04 of the frame high. `offsetY` is where they sit, as a fraction of frame height from the centre: 0.35 (the default) is near the bottom, 0 the middle, -0.35 the top.

captions.description: The captions, each shown from start to end.

end.description: When it goes, in seconds on the timeline; after start.

start.description: When it appears, in seconds on the timeline.

text.description: The words. A newline breaks the line.

offsetY.description: Vertical placement as a fraction of frame height from the centre, positive down.

style.description: The look every caption shares, as a title's style; only the fields that differ from the default are needed. Its content is replaced by each caption's text.

align.description: Line alignment within the block; see [`TextAlign`].

oneOf.description: Lines share a left edge, which is where the clip's position is.

Lines are centred on each other and on the clip's position - the
default, and what the reader falls back to for an unrecognised value.
Lines share a right edge, which is where the clip's position is.

background.description:
A solid background behind the text, `#rrggbb[aa]`; its alpha is the
background's opacity. Empty string for none. The painter and older
comments call it the plate.

backgroundPaddingX.description:
The air between the words and the background's left and right
edges, as a fraction of frame height, on an axis the words size
themselves: a box with a width is exactly that wide. The default
is the air every background had before it was a dial, 35 % of the
default size's em.

backgroundPaddingY.description: The same above and below; 20 % of the default em by default.

backgroundRadius.description:
The background's corner radius as a fraction of frame height, so a
title composed against 1080p keeps its corners at 4K. The default is
the rounding every background wore before it had a dial - 15 % of
the default size's em - and zero is square.

color.description: Fill colour as a CSS hex string, e.g. "#ffffff".

content.description:
The words themselves, newlines included. The clip's display name is
snapshotted from the first non-empty line.

fontFamily.description:
CSS-style family name, quotes included where the name needs them,
e.g. `"Cabinet Grotesk"`. May name a [`CustomFont`] the user added.

fontSize.description: Cap height as a fraction of frame height.

fontWeight.description:
CSS-scale weight, 100..=900; the reader clamps hand-edited values
into that range.

italic.description: Italic when true. A style flag, not a separate face.

lineHeight.description:
Baseline spacing as a multiple of the font size; the reader floors it
at 0.5 so lines cannot collapse onto each other.

maxHeight.description:
The box's height as a fraction of frame height; the stage's top and
bottom grips set it, and the inspector's Height field. Zero - the
default - is the words' own height. With a height the block is a
box exactly that tall, the words centred in it, so a lower third
can be a band of a fixed size whatever is written on it.
https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues/119

maxWidth.description:
The widest a line may run, as a fraction of frame width, before its
words wrap onto the next; the stage's side grips set it. Zero - the
default - is no limit: a line is as long as its words. With a limit
the block is a box exactly that wide, plate included, and the lines
align inside it.

opacity.description:
Opacity of the whole title in 0..=1, multiplied with the clip's own
opacity.

shadow.description: A drop shadow for legibility over footage. On by default.

strokeColor.description: Outline colour, only visible when `stroke_width` is non-zero.

strokeWidth.description:
Outline thickness as a fraction of frame height. Zero - the default -
means no stroke.

tracking.description:
Extra letter spacing, in the same frame-height fractions as
`font_size`. Zero is the font's natural fit.

name: clip_add
title: Place a clip
description: Places a clip of a media item (`mediaId`, from the bin) on a lane (`trackId`, from `timeline_read`) starting at `start` seconds. Its length is the media's (5 s for a still). `ripple: true` pushes later clips on that lane right instead of overlapping them. The new clip's id is `createdId`.

inputSchema.description:
Places a clip of `media_id` on a named track, minting a "c" id.
Duration comes from the media (five seconds for a still or unknown
length); errs if the media or track no longer exists.

mediaId.description: The bin item to cut from.

ripple.description:
When true and the drop would overlap something on this track,
every clip at or after `start` is shifted right by the new
clip's duration, so the drop lands without covering anything.
False for programmatic adds, true for a drop from the bin.

start.description: Timeline position in seconds, floored at 0.

trackId.description: The lane to place it on.

name: clip_frame
title: Fit or fill the frame
description: Sizes a picture to the frame in one step: `framing` "fit" shows all of it (bars where the shapes differ), "fill" covers the frame and crops the overhang. Where the clip's scale is keyframed, the key goes at `at` (a fraction of the clip, 0-1).

inputSchema.description:
Sizes a picture to the frame in one step: fitted whole inside it,
or covering it, centred either way and unstretched (see
[`crate::model::framing_scale`]; a turned picture is sized as turned).
A scale or a position with keys gets a key at `at` rather than a new
constant, the way every edit of a keyed property lands, so the rest
of the ride is left as it was. A no-op for a clip that is not a video
or a still, or whose media's size is unknown.

at.description: Where in the clip, `0..=1`, a keyed property takes its key.

clipId.description: The clip to size. An unknown id is a no-op.

oneOf.description:
The whole picture in the frame, as large as it goes: bars where the
shapes differ. Every picture's size before it is touched.

The frame covered, the picture centred and cut at the edges that
overhang it.

name: clip_mask
title: Mask a clip
description: Keeps part of a clip's picture with a shape, or with `mask: null` takes the mask off. `shape` is linear, mirror, circle, rectangle, heart or star; `x`/`y` move its centre as fractions of the picture's width/height (positive right/down); `width`/`height` are fractions of the picture's shorter side; `rotation` in degrees; `roundness` (rectangle corners) and `feather` (edge softness) 0-1; `invert` keeps the outside. Fields left out take the default circle's. Animate it with `keyframe_set` on maskX, maskY, maskWidth, maskHeight, maskRotation, maskRoundness or maskFeather.

mask.description: The shape and its numbers, or null to take the mask off.

feather.description:
How soft the edge is, `0..=1`: one fades across half the picture's
shorter side.

height.description: The box's height, on the same terms; a mirror's thickness.

invert.description: Keeps the outside of the shape instead of the inside.

rotation.description: Clockwise degrees about the mask's centre.

roundness.description: How round a rectangle's corners are, `0..=1`.

oneOf.description: The part of the picture on one side of a line through the centre.
A band along a line through the centre: the line mirrored.

An ellipse; a circle when its box is square. The default, and what
the reader falls back to.
A box, its corners rounded by the mask's `roundness`.
A heart, point down.
A five-pointed star, point up.

width.description:
The box's width, as a fraction of the picture's shorter side - the
unit that keeps a circle round on any aspect.

x.description:
The centre's offset from the picture's centre, as a fraction of the
picture's width; positive is right.

y.description: The same down the picture's height; positive is down.

name: clip_speed
title: Change a clip's speed
description: Plays a clip faster or slower: `speed` from 0.0625 to 16 (2 is double speed). The same stretch of source is kept, so the clip's length on the timeline changes.

inputSchema.description:
Changes playback rate while holding the amount of source covered
constant - the clip's timeline duration is what stretches, which is
what makes this a speed change rather than a trim.

clipId.description: The clip to retime. An unknown id is a no-op.

ripple.description:
When true - the magnetic timeline - the clips after it on its
lane move by however far its end moved, either way, so a clip
sped up closes up behind it as a magnetic trim does. False
leaves the gap; later clips then only move out of the way of a
clip that grew over them.

speed.description: The new rate, clamped into 0.0625..=16 (the engine's range).

name: clip_stabilize
title: Stabilize a clip
description: Takes the camera's shake out of a video clip, or with `stabilize: null` stops. `smoothness` 0-1 (low keeps pans and removes jitter, high leaves only the slowest moves), `maxZoom` (at least 1) is how far the picture may be enlarged to hide the moving edges, `tripod: true` locks the frame entirely. The shake is measured when the clip is previewed or exported.

inputSchema.description:
Turns a picture's stabilization on, sets its settings, or takes it
off. Tidied on the way in; see [`Stabilize::tidy`]. The camera's
movement is measured by the host the first time a clip of the
media asks for it; until then the clip shows as shot.

clipId.description: The clip. An unknown id is a no-op.

anyOf.description:
A clip's stabilization: the camera's shake taken out of the picture.

The camera's movement is measured once, frame to frame, by the host's
analysis and cached in the project folder beside the masks; these are
the settings the smooth path and the correction are worked out from,
live, whenever they change. Off is no `Stabilize` at all.

keepRotation.description:
Leave the camera's roll as shot: only its drift and its zoom are
corrected.

maxZoom.description:
The most the picture may be zoomed to hide the edges the correction
moves into view, `1..=MAX_STABILIZE_ZOOM`. The zoom used is the
least the whole clip needs, up to this; past it the correction is
eased where it would show an edge.

smoothness.description:
How much of the camera's movement is smoothed away, `0..=1`: low
keeps a pan or a glide and takes out the jitter, high leaves only
the slowest of moves. Measured on the timeline, so a clip sped up
is smoothed as calmly as one at its own pace.

tripod.description:
Lock the frame entirely, as on a tripod, rather than follow the
camera's intended move.

stabilize.description: The settings, or None to take stabilization off.

name: clip_transform
title: Place, scale or rotate a clip
description: Sets a picture's placement; only the fields given change. scale 0.05-8 (1 fits the frame), offsetX/offsetY as fractions of the frame's width/height from the centre (positive is right/down, within ±3), rotation in degrees, stretchX/stretchY 0.1-10.

inputSchema.description:
Adjusts the picture's placement. Each field is optional so a drag
can send just the axis it moved; absent fields stay put.

clipId.description: The clip to place. An unknown id is a no-op.

offsetX.description: New horizontal offset as a frame-width fraction, clamped to ±3.

offsetY.description: New vertical offset as a frame-height fraction, clamped to ±3.

rotation.description:
New rotation in degrees, wrapped into (-180, 180] so a full drag
never accumulates turns.

stretchX.description: New width multiplier beyond the scale, clamped into 0.1..=10.

stretchY.description: New height multiplier, on the same terms.

annotations.title: Place, scale or rotate a clip

name: clip_trim
title: Trim a clip
description: Moves one edge of a clip by `delta` seconds of timeline: `edge` "start" with a positive delta shortens it from the head (the picture does not slide), "end" with a positive delta lengthens it. A clip is never shorter than 1/60 s or longer than its media allows. `ripple: true` closes or opens the gap behind it on that lane.

inputSchema.description:
Drags one edge of a clip. A head trim moves the in-point with the
edge (scaled by speed) so the remaining pixels do not slide; either
edge stops at the sixtieth-of-a-second minimum duration. An unknown
clip is a no-op.

delta.description:
Signed seconds of timeline the edge moves: positive drags the
head right (shortening) or the tail right (lengthening).

oneOf.description:
The head. Trimming here moves the in-point with the edge, so the
remaining frames stay where they were on the timeline.
The tail. Trimming here only lengthens or shortens the clip.

ripple.description:
When true the lane closes up behind the trim - the magnetic
timeline. A tail trim moves every later clip on the track by
the change in length. A head trim keeps the clip where it was
(the in-point moves, the start does not) and moves every later
clip by what was cut or restored, so the trimmed clip and the
one behind it stay touching. False trims the clip alone.
https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues/106

name: clip_update
title: Change a clip
description: Changes only the fields given in `patch`: volume (gain, 1 is unchanged, may exceed 1), fadeIn/fadeOut (seconds), opacity (0-1), muted, flipH/flipV, blend, crop (fractions off each edge, null to remove), videoEffects and filters (the whole chain: a list of {id, params}; ids from `effects_list`), transitionIn ({id, duration} on the cut into the clip, null to remove), text (a title's style, null to remove), mask (see `clip_mask`), background (the clip's own background, null to follow the timeline's) and audioStream.

inputSchema.description:
Applies a [`ClipPatch`]: only the fields present change, with the
clamps documented on the patch. An unknown clip is a no-op.

patch.description: Which properties change, and to what.

audioStream.description:
Which of the media's audio streams the clip plays, by stream index:
absent leaves it alone, null goes back to the file's first, a value
names one. See `Clip::audio_stream`.

anyOf.description:
What fills the frame where the picture does not reach: the bars either
side of a wide shot in a tall frame, or the margin round a picture
scaled down. Nothing - black, as every project was before there was a
choice - a blurred, enlarged copy of the clip's own frame, a colour, or
a still from the bin.

A timeline carries one ([`Timeline::background`]) and a clip may carry
its own over it ([`Clip::background`]); which clips have one at all is
[`Timeline::background_of`]'s to say.

oneOf.description: Black: nothing drawn behind the picture.
The clip's own frame, enlarged to cover the whole frame and blurred.

amount.description:
How soft, `0..=1`: a blur of a twelfth of the frame's shorter
side at one.

oneOf.description: One flat colour, `#rrggbb`.

color.description: The colour, as a title's colours are written.

oneOf.description: A still from the bin, enlarged to cover the frame.

mediaId.description: The bin item. One that has gone, or none yet, draws nothing.

background.description:
The clip's own background over the timeline's: absent leaves it
alone, null goes back to following the timeline's, a value - black
included - is the clip's own. See `Clip::background`.

blend.description: The blend mode's name; empty is normal.

anyOf.description: A crop: what is taken off each edge, as fractions of the source.

crop.description:
The crop, same three-way wire semantics as `transition_in`: absent
leaves it alone, null takes it off, a value replaces it.

fadeIn.description: New fade-in length in seconds, floored at 0.

fadeOut.description: New fade-out length in seconds, floored at 0.

filters.description:
Wholesale replacement of the audio filter chain - the UI sends the
full list, not a diff.

items.description:
One applied audio filter or video effect: a catalogue id plus whatever
parameters were set. The catalogues themselves (and the FFmpeg strings
they build) live in the UI today; the model only stores the numbers.

enabled.description: False bypasses without losing settings. Absent means enabled.

id.description:
Which catalogue entry this is, e.g. "sepia". Not minted; an id the
catalogue no longer knows is simply skipped at render time.

items.description: One key on one parameter of an applied effect; see `AppliedFilter::keys`.

at.description: Where in the clip, as a fraction of its timeline length, `0..=1`.

ease.description: How this key is approached from the previous one.

value.description: The value there, in the parameter's own units.

keys.description:
The knobs that ride rather than hold: a sorted run of keys per
parameter name, each `at` a fraction of the clip like a `ClipKey`'s.
A parameter with keys is played from them and its `params` entry is
only what it falls back to with the keys taken off.

params.description:
The user's knob settings, keyed by parameter name. Missing keys mean
the catalogue's defaults; ordered so serialisation is stable.

anyOf.description:
A shape that keeps part of a clip's picture: CapCut's Mask. Drawn over
the picture as it is seen - after the crop and the flips, before the
placement - so it moves, scales and turns with the clip, and multiplies
with the cutout's matte and everything else that weighs the picture.

Its numbers other than the shape and the invert can be keyed, as the
placement's can (`KeyProperty::MaskX` and on); a keyed number's keys
replace the constant here.

feather.description:
How soft the edge is, `0..=1`: one fades across half the picture's
shorter side.

height.description: The box's height, on the same terms; a mirror's thickness.

invert.description: Keeps the outside of the shape instead of the inside.

rotation.description: Clockwise degrees about the mask's centre.

roundness.description: How round a rectangle's corners are, `0..=1`.

oneOf.description: The part of the picture on one side of a line through the centre.
A band along a line through the centre: the line mirrored.

An ellipse; a circle when its box is square. The default, and what
the reader falls back to.
A box, its corners rounded by the mask's `roundness`.
A heart, point down.
A five-pointed star, point up.

width.description:
The box's width, as a fraction of the picture's shorter side - the
unit that keeps a circle round on any aspect.

x.description:
The centre's offset from the picture's centre, as a fraction of the
picture's width; positive is right.

y.description: The same down the picture's height; positive is down.

mask.description:
The mask, same three-way wire semantics as `crop`: absent leaves it
alone, null takes it off, a value replaces it, tidied on the way in.
Its keys are the clip's own (`setClipKey` with `maskX` and on), and
stay when it is taken off, for a mask put back on to ride again.

muted.description:
Whether the clip's own sound is silenced: true mutes it, false lets
it play again. A detach sets this on the video it took the sound
from, so this is also how a video whose detached sound was later
deleted gets its voice back.

name.description:
New display name, taken verbatim. A later `text` patch overwrites it
with the title's first line.

preservePitch.description: New pitch-preservation setting, taken as sent.

anyOf.description:
A title's styling. Sizes are fractions of the frame, so a title composed
against 1080p lands correctly exported at 4K. A style arriving in a
command needs only the fields it changes; the rest are the default's, so
a caller can say `{ "content": "Hello" }` and get a title that looks like
one the window would place.

align.description: Line alignment within the block; see [`TextAlign`].

oneOf.description: Lines share a left edge, which is where the clip's position is.

Lines are centred on each other and on the clip's position - the
default, and what the reader falls back to for an unrecognised value.
Lines share a right edge, which is where the clip's position is.

A solid background behind the text, `#rrggbb[aa]`; its alpha is the
background's opacity. Empty string for none. The painter and older
comments call it the plate.

The air between the words and the background's left and right

Baseline spacing as a multiple of the font size; the reader floors it

The box's height as a fraction of frame height; the stage's top and

Opacity of the whole title in 0..=1, multiplied with the clip's own

id.description: Which transition from the catalogue, e.g. "cross-fade".

params.description:
The package's knobs as set on this cut, by key; a knob left out is

name: clips_add_sequence
title: Place clips end to end
description: Lays several media items (`mediaIds`, from the bin, in order) end to end starting at `start` seconds, each its media's length (5 s for a still), in one undoable step. With no `trackId` they go on the lowest lane free for the whole run; on a named lane, `ripple: true` makes room as a drop does. `createdId` is the last clip's id; `timeline_read` lists the rest.

inputSchema.description:
Several bin items one after another on one lane, as one step: what
a selection of cards dragged from the bin, or added at the playhead,
lands as. Each clip starts where the one before it ends. Naming a
lane puts the run there, each clip placed as [`Command::AddClip`]
places one with the same `ripple`; without one, the run goes on the
lowest lane free for its whole length, a new one when none is.

mediaIds.description: The bin items, in the order they are laid down.

ripple.description:
On a named lane, make room as a drop does rather than take the
nearest gap.

start.description: Where the first clip starts, in seconds, floored at 0.

trackId.description: The lane, or None for the lowest one free for the whole run.

name: clips_move
title: Move clips
description: Moves clips in one undoable step: each to a new `start` (seconds, at least 0) and `trackId`. Unknown ids are skipped.

inputSchema.description:
Repositions any number of clips in one edit - one undo step for a
whole multi-selection drag. Unknown clips and tracks are tolerated
per [`ClipMove`].

items.description: Where one clip is going, in a multi-clip move.

clipId.description:
The clip to move. An unknown id is skipped, not an error - the rest
of the batch of moves still lands.

start.description: New timeline position in seconds, floored at 0.

trackId.description:
Destination track. An unknown id moves the clip in time but leaves it
on its current track.

name: clips_remove
title: Delete clips
description: Deletes clips from the active timeline. `ripple: true` closes the gaps they leave on their lanes; false leaves the gaps.

inputSchema.description: Deletes clips from the active timeline. Unknown ids are ignored.

ripple.description:
When true the deletion leaves no gap: on each track, every clip
that starts after a removed span moves left by the length of the
removed spans before it. A track the deletion never touched
stays where it is, so a picture going from one lane does not
pull the sound on another - the magnetic track, which is
what was asked for. False leaves the hole.
https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues/106

name: clips_split
title: Split clips
description: Cuts each named clip in two at `time` seconds on the timeline. The first part keeps the id; the second gets a new one. Clips the time does not fall inside are left alone.

inputSchema.description:
Cuts each named clip in two at one playhead time. The head keeps the
id and the transition; the tail is minted fresh and stays
source-continuous. A clip the time misses (or grazes within the
minimum duration) is skipped.

clipIds.description: The clips under the playhead - normally the selection.

time.description: The cut point, in timeline seconds.

name: concat_version
title: Concat version
description: What this Concat speaks: the API version, the build, its capabilities, and how this MCP server reaches it (`mcp.mode`: "window" when it goes through the open Concat window's server, "headless" when it runs the editor engine itself). Call it first if unsure what is available.

inputSchema.description:
The API's version, the build behind it, and what that build
serves. The one method to call first: its reply's `capabilities`
names the transports and optional features this server has, so a
caller knows what to ask for before it asks.

name: edit_apply
title: Apply an edit
description: Applies any one edit command to an open project, as one undoable step. `command` is an object tagged by `op` - every edit the window can make is one, with the same limits and refusals; the typed tools below are the common ones. `{"op": "batch", "commands": [...]}` applies several commands as one atomic, undoable step: all land or none does, and `createdId` is the last id minted inside. A refusal comes back as the sentence the window would show, with nothing changed. Returns the project summary; a command that creates something puts its id in `createdId`.

AppliedFilter.description: One applied audio filter or video effect: a catalogue id plus whatever parameters were set.

id.description: Which catalogue entry this is, e.g.

The edit. Boxed because a command is the largest thing a

description: Steps an open project's history back one edit (a batch is one edit).

inputSchema.description: Steps the history back one edit.

name: effect_key_set
title: Animate an effect parameter
description: Puts a key on one parameter (`key`, from `effects_list`) of one effect in a clip's chain (`entry`, its index in the clip's videoEffects, from 0) at `at` (a fraction of the clip's length, 0-1), holding `value` in the parameter's own units. Keep the value within the range `effects_list` gives.

inputSchema.description:
Puts a key on one parameter of one link of a clip's picture chain,
replacing whichever key on it was already within a hair of `at`.
The value is the parameter's own; the package's range is the
caller's to keep, the model not knowing it.

ease.description: How the key is approached from the one before it.

entry.description:
Which link, as an index into `video_effects`. Out of range is a
no-op.

name: effect_layer_add
title: Add an effect layer
description: Places an effect or look as a layer over the timeline: from `start` for `duration` seconds (5 s when absent), it treats everything beneath it. `effectId` is a package id from `effects_list`; the layer's opacity (via `clip_update`) is how strongly it applies. To put an effect on one clip instead, set that clip's `videoEffects` with `clip_update`.

inputSchema.description:
Places a layer: a look or an effect over a span of the timeline that
treats everything beneath it. No media; the chain starts as the one
package named, at its defaults, and the clip's opacity is how hard it
is applied.

duration.description: Seconds on the timeline; the editorial default when absent.

effectId.description: The package the layer applies, e.g. "concat.warm".

start.description: Timeline position in seconds, floored at 0.

trackId.description:
The lane to place it on. None picks the first free lane *above*
the highest one occupied over its span, minting one at the top
when every lane above is taken: a layer treats what is beneath
it, so one under the picture would treat nothing.

name: effects_list
title: List effects
description: Every effect package this build has - id, name, kind ("effect", "filter", "audio", "transition" or "generator"), category and each parameter's key, range, default and unit - so an effect chain, a layer or a transition can be built correctly. `kind` narrows the list.

inputSchema.description:
Every effect package the build knows, with its parameters, so a
caller can build a valid chain without reading a manifest.

name: export_cancel
title: Cancel an export
description: Stops a running export job at its next frame; it then ends as "cancelled".

inputSchema.description:
Stops a running export at its next frame. The job then ends with
[`Event::ExportFailed`] carrying [`ErrorCode::Cancelled`].

name: export_start
title: Start an export
description: Starts rendering an open project's active timeline to `output` (an .mp4 path), as the window's Export does. Returns at once with a `job` id; follow it with `export_wait` or `export_status`. Optional: crf (quality, lower is better, 20 by default), preset (x264 speed, "medium"), width/height, rateNum/rateDen, codec ("h264", "hevc" or "av1"), tenBit, colorRange, hdr. One export runs at a time; another is refused as busy.

inputSchema.description:
Renders an open project's active timeline to a file, exactly as
the window's Export does: cutouts analysed, stabilized clips'
camera shake measured, titles painted, then the
frame loop and the mix. Returns at once with the job's name; the
render runs on its own thread and reports through [`Event`]s, ending
in [`Event::ExportDone`] or [`Event::ExportFailed`]. One export runs
at a time; a second is refused as [`ErrorCode::Busy`].

codec.description:
"h264", "hevc" or "av1". H.264 when absent - HEVC for an HDR file,
which H.264 does not carry.

colorRange.description:
"limited" (16-235, what every player and YouTube expect) or "full"
(0-255, for screen content bound for a PC player that reads the
tag). Limited when absent.
https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues/103

crf.description: Constant rate factor; lower is better and bigger. 20 when absent.

hdr.description:
For an HDR timeline: written as HDR, its own HLG or PQ in ten bits
(true, the default), or tone-mapped to SDR (false). Nothing for an
SDR timeline.

height.description: Output height; the timeline's when absent.

preset.description: The x264 preset name. "medium" when absent.

rateDen.description: Frame rate denominator; the timeline's when absent.

rateNum.description: Frame rate numerator; the timeline's when absent.

tenBit.description: Ten bits a channel. Eight when absent.

width.description: Output width; the timeline's when absent.

name: export_status
title: Export status
description: How an export job stands, at once: `state` ("running", "done", "cancelled" or "failed"), `stage` ("cutout", "stabilize", "video", "audio", "mux"), frames done of total, `fraction` of the stage (0-1), and once done the file and its size, or the error.

inputSchema.description:
How a job stands: running and how far along, or how it ended. The
same news the events carry, for a caller that was not listening
when it came; the last few finished jobs are remembered.

name: export_wait
title: Wait for an export
description: Waits for an export job to end, up to `timeoutSeconds` (60 by default, 600 at most), reporting progress as it goes, and returns its status as `export_status` does. If it is still running when the time is up, call it again.

inputSchema.description:
How a job stands: running and how far along, or how it ended. The
same news the events carry, for a caller that was not listening
when it came; the last few finished jobs are remembered.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait, in seconds.

name: keyframe_clear
title: Remove a keyframe
description: Removes the key on `property` at `at` (a fraction of the clip's length), if there is one.

inputSchema.description:
Takes the key at `at` off one property, if there is one there. The
other half of the diamond: a filled diamond clicked is this.

at.description: Where in the clip the key to remove sits, `0..=1`.

oneOf.description: `Clip::scale`.
`Clip::offset_x`.
`Clip::offset_y`.
`Clip::rotation`.
`Clip::opacity`.
`Clip::volume`.
`ClipMask::x`.
`ClipMask::y`.
`ClipMask::width`.
`ClipMask::height`.
`ClipMask::rotation`.
`ClipMask::roundness`.
`ClipMask::feather`.

name: keyframe_set
title: Set a keyframe
description: Animates a clip: puts a key on `property` (scale, offsetX, offsetY, rotation, opacity, volume, or a mask's maskX, maskY, maskWidth, maskHeight, maskRotation, maskRoundness, maskFeather) at `at`, a fraction of the clip's length from 0 (its start) to 1 (its end), holding `value` in the property's own units - the number the inspector shows. A key already within a hair of `at` is replaced. `ease` is how the value is approached: [x1, y1, x2, y2] like a CSS cubic-bezier, linear when absent.

inputSchema.description:
Puts a key on one property at one point of a clip, replacing
whichever key on that property was already within a hair of it.

The value is the property's own - the number the inspector shows -
not the relative factor the engine plays; see `model::ClipKey`.

ease.description: How the key is approached from the one before it.

oneOf.description: `Clip::scale`.
`Clip::offset_x`.
`Clip::offset_y`.
`Clip::rotation`.
`Clip::opacity`.
`Clip::volume`.
`ClipMask::x`.
`ClipMask::y`.
`ClipMask::width`.
`ClipMask::height`.
`ClipMask::rotation`.

`ClipMask::feather`.

name: media_import
title: Import media
description: Adds a file (an absolute path) to an open project's media bin, as dropping it on the window does. The new item's id is the summary's `createdId`; place it on the timeline with `clip_add`. Importing a path already in the bin changes nothing.

inputSchema.description:
Probes a file and adds it to a project's bin: what dropping a file
on the window does. A path already in the bin is a no-op.

name: media_probe
title: Probe a media file
description: Reports what is inside a video, audio or image file - duration in seconds, streams, frame size and rate, codecs - without changing any project.

inputSchema.description: Reports what is inside a media file without touching any project.

name: preview_frame
title: Preview a frame
description: Renders the true composited frame at `time` seconds on an open project's timeline and returns it as an image to look at - titles, effects and transforms included. Without `width` and `height` it fits within 1280 pixels; give both for another size (8192 at most). With `output` (a .png path) it is written there instead.

inputSchema.description:
Composites the true frame at one instant. Written as a PNG to
`output` when there is one, and handed back inline as a
[`Picture`] otherwise, for a caller on the far side of a socket.

height.description: Frame height; the timeline's when absent.

output.description: The file to write; absent means the picture comes back inline.

width.description: Frame width; the timeline's when absent.

name: project_close
title: Close a project
description: Closes an open project. With `save: true` it is saved first; otherwise unsaved edits are dropped.

inputSchema.description:
Closes an open project, saving first when asked. Unsaved edits are
dropped otherwise.

save.description: Whether to write the document before closing.

name: project_create
title: Create a project
description: Creates a project folder named `name` inside the existing directory `location`, and opens it. `video` sets the frame and rate (1920×1080 at 30 fps when absent). Returns the project summary; its folder is `location/name`, which is the `path` later tools take. Refuses a folder that already holds a project.

inputSchema.description:
Creates a project folder under `location`, named `name`, and opens
it. Refuses a folder that already holds a project.

location.description: The directory the project folder is made in.

name.description: The project's name; the folder is named after it.

anyOf.description:
A timeline's output frame, rate and colour.

The same four numbers the document's top-level `video` block has always
carried, now one set per timeline, and the colour it is output in. The
top-level block is still written, as the active timeline's frame and
rate, so a build that predates this reads the document it always did,
and a document from such a build gives every timeline that block on the
way in.

colorSpace.description:
The colour the timeline is output in: SDR for every timeline from
before HDR, and until its first HDR clip (see
`Editor::follow_first_hdr`). Left out of the document for SDR, so
those documents stay as they were.

oneOf.description: Rec. 709, SDR: every timeline until its first HDR clip.

Rec. 2020 with HLG: what an iPhone records, and what a timeline
becomes on its first HDR clip.
Rec. 2020 with PQ: HDR10.

rateDen.description: Denominator of the frame rate, e.g. 1001 for 29.97 fps.

rateNum.description: Numerator of the frame rate, e.g. 30000 for 29.97 fps.

video.description: Frame and rate; 1080p at 30 when absent.

name: project_get
title: Get the whole project
description: An open project's full state: every timeline, clip field, media item and setting, as the editor holds it. Large; `timeline_read` is usually enough.

inputSchema.description: The state of an open project.

name: project_list
title: Recent projects
description: The projects this machine opened most recently, newest first: each one's folder `path`, name, frame size and rate. A project is a folder; every other project tool names it by that `path`.

inputSchema.description: The projects this machine opened most recently, newest first.

name: project_open
title: Open a project
description: Opens a project folder so it can be read and edited. Opening one already open returns it as it stands, unsaved edits included. Refused when the Concat window has that project open. Returns the project summary.

inputSchema.description:
Opens a project folder. Opening one already open returns its state
as it stands, edits and all.

name: project_save
title: Save a project
description: Writes an open project's document to its folder; edits are only in memory until this is called. `name` renames the project as it saves.

inputSchema.description: Writes the document to the project folder.

name.description: A new name for the project, when renaming.

name: project_set_video
title: Set frame size and rate
description: Sets the active timeline's frame (width, height in pixels) and rate (rateNum/rateDen frames a second, e.g. 30000/1001 for 29.97) as one undoable edit.

inputSchema.description: Sets the active timeline's frame and rate, as an undoable edit.

colorSpace.description:
The colour the timeline is output in: SDR for every timeline from
before HDR, and until its first HDR clip (see
`Editor::follow_first_hdr`). Left out of the document for SDR, so
those documents stay as they were.

oneOf.description: Rec. 709, SDR: every timeline until its first HDR clip.

Rec. 2020 with HLG: what an iPhone records, and what a timeline
becomes on its first HDR clip.
Rec. 2020 with PQ: HDR10.

rateDen.description: Denominator of the frame rate, e.g. 1001 for 29.97 fps.

rateNum.description: Numerator of the frame rate, e.g. 30000 for 29.97 fps.

name: template_instantiate
title: Make a project from a template
description: Makes a project from a template - `template` (its folder), `location` and `name` as for `project_create` - with every slot filled by a file (`fills`: [{mediaId, file}]). Opens it and returns its summary.

inputSchema.description:
Makes a project from a template with every slot filled, and opens
it. Every slot must be filled; a set that leaves one empty makes
nothing.

items.description: One template slot and the file that takes it.

file.description: The file to put there; probed on the way in.

mediaId.description: The placeholder's media id in the template.

location.description: The directory the project folder is made in.

annotations.title: Make a project from a template

name: template_list
title: List templates
description: The template library: each template's folder, name and the slots (placeholder media ids) a project made from it must fill.

inputSchema.description: The template library.

name: timeline_background
title: Set the background
description: Sets what shows behind pictures that do not cover the frame, on a whole timeline (`timelineId` from `timeline_read`): `{"kind": "none"}` (black), `{"kind": "blur", "amount": 0-1}` (the clip itself, enlarged and blurred), `{"kind": "color", "color": "#rrggbb"}` or `{"kind": "image", "mediaId": ...}`. One clip's own background is `clip_update`'s `background`.

inputSchema.description:
Sets what fills a timeline's frame behind the pictures on its lowest
picture lane; see `Timeline::background_of`. Tidied first: an amount
held to `0..=1`, a colour that does not read made black.

oneOf.description: Black: nothing drawn behind the picture.
The clip's own frame, enlarged to cover the whole frame and blurred.

amount.description:
How soft, `0..=1`: a blur of a twelfth of the frame's shorter
side at one.

oneOf.description: One flat colour, `#rrggbb`.

color.description: The colour, as a title's colours are written.

oneOf.description: A still from the bin, enlarged to cover the frame.

mediaId.description: The bin item. One that has gone, or none yet, draws nothing.

timelineId.description: The timeline. An unknown id is a no-op.

name: timeline_read
title: Read the timeline
description: An open project's active timeline as a compact summary: frame size and fps, the lanes (`tracks`, top to bottom, with their ids), every clip in time order with its id, kind, track, start, duration and end in seconds and whatever is not at its default (speed, volume, opacity, transform, effects, keyframed properties, text), and the media bin with each item's id. Read this to learn the ids other tools need.

inputSchema.description: The state of an open project.

name: title_add
title: Add a title
description: Places a title (text over the picture) at `start` seconds for `duration` seconds (4 s when absent). `style` sets the words and look - `content`, `fontFamily`, `fontSize` (fraction of frame height, 0.09 by default), `fontWeight` (100-900), `color` ("#rrggbb"), `align`, `background`, `strokeWidth`... - and needs only the fields that differ from the default. `offsetY` places it vertically as a fraction of frame height from the centre (positive is down). With no `trackId` and `above: true` it lands on a lane above the picture. The new clip's id is `createdId`.

inputSchema.description:
Places a title: a clip with no media behind it, named after the
text's first line, minting a "c" id.

above.description:
When `track_id` is None and this is true, the clip lands on the
first free lane *above* the highest one occupied over its span,
minting a new lane at the top when every one above is taken.
What the editor sets for a caption and for a title alike, so
words sit over the video rather than under it; false keeps the
bottom-first walk of [`Command::AddClipAtFirstFree`]. Ignored
when `track_id` names a track.

duration.description:
Seconds on the timeline; the editorial default when absent. Here
so a caption run can land as one batch instead of add-then-trim
per clip - a batch cannot trim a clip whose id it cannot know yet.

offsetY.description:
Vertical placement as a frame-height fraction, clamped like
SetClipTransform. Lower thirds are made of this.

start.description: Timeline position in seconds, floored at 0.

anyOf.description:
A title's styling. Sizes are fractions of the frame, so a title composed
against 1080p lands correctly exported at 4K. A style arriving in a
command needs only the fields it changes; the rest are the default's, so
a caller can say `{ "content": "Hello" }` and get a title that looks like
one the window would place.

align.description: Line alignment within the block; see [`TextAlign`].

oneOf.description: Lines share a left edge, which is where the clip's position is.

Lines are centred on each other and on the clip's position - the
default, and what the reader falls back to for an unrecognised value.
Lines share a right edge, which is where the clip's position is.

background.description:
A solid background behind the text, `#rrggbb[aa]`; its alpha is the
background's opacity. Empty string for none. The painter and older
comments call it the plate.

backgroundPaddingX.description:
The air between the words and the background's left and right
edges, as a fraction of frame height, on an axis the words size
themselves: a box with a width is exactly that wide. The default
is the air every background had before it was a dial, 35 % of the
default size's em.

backgroundPaddingY.description: The same above and below; 20 % of the default em by default.

backgroundRadius.description:
The background's corner radius as a fraction of frame height, so a
title composed against 1080p keeps its corners at 4K. The default is
the rounding every background wore before it had a dial - 15 % of
the default size's em - and zero is square.

color.description: Fill colour as a CSS hex string, e.g. "#ffffff".

content.description:
The words themselves, newlines included. The clip's display name is
snapshotted from the first non-empty line.

fontFamily.description:
CSS-style family name, quotes included where the name needs them,
e.g. `"Cabinet Grotesk"`. May name a [`CustomFont`] the user added.

fontSize.description: Cap height as a fraction of frame height.

fontWeight.description:
CSS-scale weight, 100..=900; the reader clamps hand-edited values
into that range.

italic.description: Italic when true. A style flag, not a separate face.

lineHeight.description:
Baseline spacing as a multiple of the font size; the reader floors it
at 0.5 so lines cannot collapse onto each other.

maxHeight.description:
The box's height as a fraction of frame height; the stage's top and
bottom grips set it, and the inspector's Height field. Zero - the
default - is the words' own height. With a height the block is a
box exactly that tall, the words centred in it, so a lower third
can be a band of a fixed size whatever is written on it.
https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues/119

maxWidth.description:
The widest a line may run, as a fraction of frame width, before its
words wrap onto the next; the stage's side grips set it. Zero - the
default - is no limit: a line is as long as its words. With a limit
the block is a box exactly that wide, plate included, and the lines
align inside it.

opacity.description:
Opacity of the whole title in 0..=1, multiplied with the clip's own
opacity.

shadow.description: A drop shadow for legibility over footage. On by default.

strokeColor.description: Outline colour, only visible when `stroke_width` is non-zero.

strokeWidth.description:
Outline thickness as a fraction of frame height. Zero - the default -
means no stroke.

tracking.description:
Extra letter spacing, in the same frame-height fractions as
`font_size`. Zero is the font's natural fit.

style.description: The words and their look. None means [`TextStyle::default`].

trackId.description:
The lane to place it on. None picks the first free track like
[`Command::AddClipAtFirstFree`]; naming a vanished track errs.

name: track_add
title: Add a lane
description: Adds a lane to the active timeline: on top, or with `bottom: true` under every other. Its id is `createdId`.

inputSchema.description:
Adds a lane, minting a "t" id: on top of the stack, or with
`bottom` under every other lane. Absent is the top, which is what
the command did before it could do anything else.

bottom.description: Under every other lane rather than on top of them.
